header.symptom: spam folder at Outlook and some Gmail, Outlook bounces, clicks down this month
header.headline: No mail is signed with teashop.example and the domain has no DMARC record, so Microsoft refuses it (6.42% of Outlook-family mail bounced) and Gmail defers part of it. The repair starts with three DNS changes today.

scorecard.key: 2 SPF records, no DMARC, DKIM d=mail42.atl11.mcsv.net
scorecard.why: SPF and DKIM pass only on Mailchimp's domain; nothing aligns with teashop.example.

scorecard.key: Gmail peak 20,965 a day, Microsoft peak 7,226 a day
scorecard.why: A bulk sender at all three providers, missing DMARC and alignment; unsubscribe headers and TLS pass.
Microsoft is refusing the mail (5.7.515); Gmail's spam rate can't be read until DKIM aligns.
A third of the audience never clicked and joined more than 180 days ago; every campaign went to everyone.
The domain is verified in Mailchimp but not authenticated, so Mailchimp signs with its own domain.
Needs DMARC at quarantine or reject with pct=100.
Authenticating the domain makes teashop.example a new signing identity at every provider.

authentication.evidence: 2 v=spf1 records on teashop.example: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all | v=spf1 include:servers.mcsv.net ?all
authentication.why: Two SPF records make every SPF check on the domain a permanent error, including Google Workspace staff mail.
The second record ends in ?all (neutral), which tells receivers nothing.

authentication.evidence: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all: 4 lookups (includes resolved); v=spf1 include:servers.mcsv.net ?all: 1 lookup (includes resolved)
authentication.why: Even merged, the two records need 5 lookups, inside the limit of 10.

authentication.evidence: TXT k2._domainkey.teashop.example: no record; TXT k3._domainkey.teashop.example: no record
authentication.why: The selectors Mailchimp's Domains page gives for this domain return nothing, so no mail is signed with teashop.example.
No DMARC record: a bulk-sender requirement at Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft, and no reports on who sends as the domain.

authentication.evidence: From teashop.example; DKIM d=mail42.atl11.mcsv.net; SPF Return-Path mail42.atl11.mcsv.net
authentication.why: SPF and DKIM both pass, but on Mailchimp's domain. Nothing matches the From domain, which is what the providers test.

sunset_rule.group: subscribed members with no click who opted in before 2026-05-01
sunset_rule.rule: 2 re-permission emails a week apart with one keep-me-subscribed button; anyone who doesn't click within 14 days of the second email stops getting campaigns; re-check every quarter.

bimi.path: possible from step 7 (DMARC p=quarantine, pct=100); needs a VMC or CMC and an SVG Tiny PS logo

ramp_up.why: DKIM moves from Mailchimp's domain to teashop.example, which has no sending history.
ramp_up.target_is: the whole subscribed audience (every campaign went to everyone) minus the sunset group
ramp_up.start: the weekday after the DNS changes in steps 1 to 3 are confirmed; dated here as if they are confirmed today
ramp_up.rule: day 1 = 10% of the target (at least 1,000), then 1.5 times the day before on each weekday, capped at the target
ramp_up.gates: move up only when bounces are at or under 2% and complaints under 0.1% at every provider with no 4.7.28 deferrals; otherwise hold 2 days; at 0.3% complaints or a block, drop back one step

repair_sequence.priority: what makes providers reject mail now
repair_sequence.do: Replace the two SPF records with one: v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:servers.mcsv.net ~all
repair_sequence.recheck: dig +short TXT teashop.example shows exactly one v=spf1 line (5 lookups); a staff email from Google Workspace shows spf=pass in its headers.

repair_sequence.priority: what makes providers reject mail now
repair_sequence.do: Add the two DKIM CNAME records from Mailchimp's Domains page (k2._domainkey and k3._domainkey), then click Authenticate in Mailchimp.
repair_sequence.recheck: list_verified_domains shows authenticated true and status AUTHENTICATED; a new Gmail test send shows dkim=pass header.i=@teashop.example.

repair_sequence.priority: what makes providers reject mail now
repair_sequence.recheck: dig +short TXT _dmarc.teashop.example returns the record; the next test send shows dmarc=pass; daily aggregate reports start arriving at the rua address.

repair_sequence.do: Watch Gmail's spam rate in Postmaster Tools now that mail is signed with teashop.example.
repair_sequence.recheck: Postmaster Tools shows a daily spam rate within days of the DKIM change; it stays under 0.1% for 7 days in a row.

repair_sequence.do: Stop sending campaigns to the whole audience: build a segment that leaves out the 15,720 never-clickers and send every campaign to it.
repair_sequence.recheck: list_campaigns shows a segment_text on every new campaign.

repair_sequence.do: Send re-permission email 1 to the sunset group (15,720 never-clickers), a week after the ramp ends; email 2 on 2026-11-20.
repair_sequence.recheck: On 2026-12-04, everyone in the group who didn't click is moved out of campaign sends; the never-clicker share drops under 20%.

repair_sequence.do: Run the ramp-up in area 7 (7 weekday steps to 31,830), top-rated members first, never the sunset group.
repair_sequence.recheck: On each step's send, Microsoft bounces back under 2% (now 6.42%) with no 5.7.515, Gmail bounces at or under 1% (now 1.49%) with no 4.7.32, and complaints under 0.1% at Yahoo and Microsoft.

repair_sequence.do: If 4 weeks of DMARC aggregate reports show only Google Workspace and Mailchimp sending as the domain, change the policy to p=quarantine; pct=100.
repair_sequence.recheck: dig +short TXT _dmarc.teashop.example shows p=quarantine; reports show no legitimate mail failing.

repair_sequence.do: After 4 more clean weeks, change the policy to p=reject.
repair_sequence.recheck: Reports keep showing only known senders passing; nothing legitimate is rejected.

repair_sequence.do: Once DMARC is at quarantine with pct=100, decide on BIMI: a Verified Mark Certificate needs a registered trademark for the logo; a Common Mark Certificate doesn't. Prepare the logo as SVG Tiny PS.
repair_sequence.recheck: dig +short TXT default._bimi.teashop.example returns a record with l= and a=; the logo shows in Gmail.
